decisions.reason: The viral-style direction does not change the established source or format of the customer testimonials.
Viral styling may support the conversion objective, but it does not change the existing performance objective or target CPL.
Permission to revise the script for viral impact does not necessarily change the requirement to use the winning creative's validated structural principles.
The viral content direction does not alter the established requirements for realistic, native-looking handheld UGC visuals.
The script-keyword and revision rule from this message is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE Event.
The viral-style instruction does not change the video count, duration, aspect ratios, or other output-package attributes.
The casting instruction contained in the source message is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE Event.
Allowing script revision for viral impact does not change the freelancer's full-service production responsibility or supplied elements.
The creative's viral style has no necessary effect on the deferred landing-page and tracking audit.
